title: Compliance portfolio shipments and tenant summary digests
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers need a predictable, auditable delivery of compliance artifacts that reflect per-tenant residency and retention policies. Current ad-hoc exports (one-off zips, ad-hoc SQL dumps) are brittle and lack standardized templates, signed manifests, and repeatable scheduling. Goal: deliver a tenant-scoped "portfolio" feature that produces a packaged monthly digest containing PDF-certified summaries, CSV forensic exports, and a machine-readable manifest; support push delivery (S3/FTP/webhook), tenant subscription preferences, and retention-aware slicing so exports never include data outside of allowed residency windows.
acceptance_criteria: Platform can generate a tenant portfolio package (PDF summary + CSV data + manifest.json) for any tenant on demand and on schedule
Packages respect tenant data residency and retention filters (no records older/newer than allowed by tenant policy)
Generated PDF includes signed checksum and version stamp; manifest contains export provenance (timestamps, dataset hashes, generating runtime version)
Delivery channels: S3 push, secure FTP, and webhook with retry/backoff; at least one channel configurable per-tenant
Console UI: tenant admins can configure cadence (daily/weekly/monthly), include/exclude datasets, and preview next scheduled export
Audit logs and per-export events are visible in Console tracing and available via API (idempotent export IDs)
End-to-end e2e test coverage for scheduling, retention slicing, and delivery retries exists in CI
out_of_scope: Building a new signing HSM — we'll integrate existing KMS/HSM flows
Ad hoc per-record redaction logic for regulated customers (handled separately as redaction pipeline)
notes: We will reuse the existing export worker infra from ENG-41230 but add a residency filter step upstream
Template responsibility: Product will author initial PDF/CSV templates; Design to provide layouts and accessibility checks
Will use s3://redwood-compliance-exports in staging for early integration tests
Security review gate required before GA — see 'security_review_required' flag
Performance: export generation should not impact online serving SLOs — job workers are rate-limited and run in separate capacity pools

implementation_notes: Manifest will follow a simple lineage schema: export_id, tenant_id, export_time, generator_version, file_entries[] (name, sha256, size_bytes)
PDFs generated using headless rendering of an accessible HTML template; CSVs streamed from row iterator
Retention filters applied as WHERE clauses in export queries and validated against tenant policy cache before generation
Delivery uses a push-first model; if push fails, package persisted and retry schedule exponential backoff up to 7 days

Integration tests for manifest checksums and KMS signature validation

Load test to validate large export throughput and worker isolation
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal tenants only (security & compliance teams); monitor delivery success and CPU/memory patterns
Beta: opt-in external customers with <5TB tenant datasets; open support channel for early feedback
GA: broad availability in hosted and dedicated; tenants in restricted regions may require additional routing rules
Feature flag gating and rate limiting during rollout to protect serving capacity
